text: PEPRMT-Tidal one-dimensional process-based model predicts gross primary productivity, ecosystem respiration methane exchange tidal wetlands daily time step. plan use model code data provided repository please cite Oikawa et al. (2024). package contains files needed run PEPRMT-Tidal, updated version PEPRMT model. model described detail Oikawa et al. (2024).

title: Peatland Ecosystem Photosynthesis, Respiration and Methane Transport model
text: Originally PEPRMT (Peatland Ecosystem Photosynthesis Methane Transport) model parameterized restored freshwater wetlands Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta, CA, USA (Oikawa et al. 2017). Presented updated version works tidal wetlands (Oikawa et al. 2024). PEPRMT modules use input structure, variables daily time step. Modules run succession, first GPP, Reco last CH4. GPP: GPP module using light use efficiency equation predict GPP. GPP can predicted using leaf area index (LAI) greenness index Phenocam data, remote sensing EVI NDVI. PEPRMT-Tidal applied Oikawa et al. (2024) uses EVI Landsat. Reco: Reco module uses Dual Arrhenius Michaelis-Menten (DAMM) approach predict Reco two carbon pools. CH4: CH4 module also uses DAMM approach includes inhibition factors decrease CH4 production presence NO3 SO4

title: Peatland Ecosystem Photosynthesis, Respiration and Methane Transport model
text: included example dataset used Oikawa et al. (2024), sources data Ameriflux eddy covariance towers across United States. data filtered gapfilled following methods outlined Oikawa et al. 2023. Ancillary data local tidal streams included continuous NO3 salinity measurements also included.

title: Methane Exchange (CH4) — PEPRMT_CH4
text: Runs PEPRMT methane production transport module freshwater peatlands tidal wetlands daily time step. Default parameter values determined via MCMC Bayesian fitting (Oikawa et al. 2024). PEPRMT model originally parameterized restored freshwater wetlands Sacramento–San Joaquin River Delta, California, USA (Oikawa et al. 2017) later updated tidal wetlands inhibition methane production response salinity nitrate (Oikawa et al. 2024). Modules intended run sequentially: PEPRMT_GPP, PEPRMT_Reco, PEPRMT_CH4. variables expected daily time step. PEPRMT modules use input structure, although variables used every module. Required data columns: Continuous day year Discontinuous day year Year Air temperature (°C) Water table depth (cm) PAR (µmol m^-2 d^-1) Leaf Area Index Greenness Index FPAR flag Light Use Efficiency Wetland age (years) Salinity (ppt) NO3 (mg L^-1) Soil organic matter (g C m^-3) Site identifier Modeled GPP (g C m^-2 day^-1) Modeled Reco (g C m^-2 day^-1) Net ecosystem exchange (g C m^-2 day^-1)

text: data Data frame containing 16 required columns used model inputs. See Details expected column structure. wetland_type Integer indicating wetland class: 1 = Freshwater peatland, 2 = Tidal wetland. Ea_SOM – Activation energy controlling temperature sensitivity decomposition soil organic matter (SOM) pool (kJ mol^-1). kM_SOM – Half-saturation constant microbial decomposition SOM pool (g C m^-3 soil). Ea_labile – Activation energy controlling temperature sensitivity decomposition labile carbon pool (kJ mol^-1). kM_labile – Half-saturation constant microbial decomposition labile carbon pool (g C m^-3 soil).
